attempts.rationale: Test a weighted combination using inverse error weights on the full pool, motivated by the combination_hint "weighted" and moderate ranking stability.
trend_dominated, moderate ranking stability suggests a robust aggregation like median could be useful.
Test a weighted combination with a different weight scheme (softmax_neg_error) to see if a smoother weighting improves over the hard inverse_error.
The series has a very strong trend and moderate ranking stability, so a robust aggregation like trimmed mean may reduce influence of outliers and correlated errors.
The series has moderate ranking stability and a strong trend; a simple DBA might capture that trend structure better than weighted mean.
trend_dominated and moderate ranking stability suggest a simple aggregation like mean could be competitive; test mean over full pool.
test a per‑horizon weighted scheme (best_per_horizon) to see if different models dominate at different lags in this trend‑dominated series.
Test weighted combination using the top‑k per‑horizon weights (w5) to see if per‑horizon averaging improves over overall weighted mean, given moderate ranking stability and strong trend.
test a forward‑selection weighted combination (w6) to see if a data‑driven subset improves over the current median leader.
The series has a strong trend and moderate ranking stability; a per‑horizon weighted mean of the top‑k models (w7) might capture subtle horizon‑specific strengths that a global weighted mean missed.
ranking stability is moderate and several models share correlated errors; a per‑horizon best‑model weighting on the top‑7 pool may capture subtle horizon differences.

decision.justification: Selected 'mean on pool4' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.1858. Series context: trend strength 0.9938 and seasonal strength 0.0896; model ranking is moderate across windows (Kendall tau 0.423); 6 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 23.835.
